judge_framing.intro: You are grading a reconnaissance report against a known ground-truth list of items the report was required to surface. Return STRICT JSON only — no prose, no markdown fences.
judge_framing.gt_heading: Ground-truth items the report had to surface
judge_framing.negative_note: (none — this is a NEGATIVE task: there was nothing relevant to surface, so every item below goes to residue)
judge_framing.match_rule:
SAME item — the same file, learning, handoff, rule or inventory entry, surfaced for the
   reason the ground truth states. Each item's title begins with the report section it came
   from; a path offered under the wrong section (an exemplar listed as a likely-touched file)
   is NOT a match, because the two sections make different claims about it.
judge_framing.plausible_real:
a real, correctly-cited item that is genuinely relevant to this
     task, just not on the ground-truth list
judge_framing.noise:
a file, learning, rule or helper that does not exist in the tree, or one with no
     bearing on this task
judge_framing.nitpick: real and correctly cited, but of no consequence to the change

noise_floor_note: UPPER BOUND, single-judge. Measured by EXP-015's A-vs-A: the combined `noise` axis swung 1.33 findings/task between IDENTICAL champion arms at an MDE of 1.50, while `noise_strict` moved 0.00 -> 0.33. Every trial behind that figure was scored by ONE judge call, and the audit modules later showed single-call residue bucketing swinging ~1.5/task on identical input (score.sh --judge-votes) — the same order as this band, so most of the 1.33 is likely judge taste rather than executor behavior. That is the same conclusion EXP-015 reached from its own numbers, and it is why this module reads `noise_strict` for verdicts. Re-measure with a panel before reading a near-threshold result on the combined axis.
